gauntlet: done summary

### What is broken

Opening `/widgets/` shows page not found (404) instead of the widgets page; `/widgets` opens it.

### Why it is broken

The part that matches web addresses to pages compares them exactly, so the final slash in `/widgets/` prevents a match. A local test reproduced the failure, and testing the explanation did not disprove it.

### How to fix it

Remove the final slash before comparing addresses so `/widgets/` and `/widgets` both open the page. The existing ticket https://github.com/example/widgets/issues/42 already covers this problem. No new ticket was created, and follow-up continues on that ticket.

gauntlet: done summary

### What is broken

Opening `/widgets/` returns page not found (404) instead of a successful response (200).

### Why it is broken

The code that matches web addresses to pages compares paths without removing the trailing slash. Local reproduction confirmed the failure, and the test of this explanation supported it.

### How to fix it

Remove the trailing slash before matching paths so `/widgets/` reaches the page. Follow-up is covered by existing ticket [#42](https://github.com/example/widgets/issues/42). No new ticket was created and no tracker state was changed.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps everything Before kept and gains two facts: it explains 404 as page not found on first use, drops the `src/router.ts:88` citation that a reader of a terminal summary never needs to open, and delivers the fixed three-section shape ending on the existing ticket with no status or evidence after it. Two small risks to tighten in the wording: the ticket link sits in the middle of its sentence rather than trailing the claim (prefer 'The existing ticket already covers this problem: https://github.com/example/widgets/issues/42'), and 'testing the explanation did not disprove it' is still a half-translated falsification test; stating it by changed input and observed result (e.g. 'opening `/widgets` without the slash returned the page, so the slash is the cause') would satisfy the first-use rule more robustly without adding words or exceeding the 180-word cap.

Two small refinements would make the contract more robust: the phrase 'the test of this explanation supported it' still gestures at investigation shorthand rather than stating the changed input and observed result (e.g. 'requesting `/widgets` without the slash returned 200, confirming the slash is the cause'); and because this summary carries a returned existing ticket, the wording could direct the third heading to be 'What happens next' (or let 'How to fix it' explicitly lead with the ticket) so the next-step reading of the returned reference is unambiguous rather than appended after a literal fix instruction.
